item.title: Hooda ready to face Nanovu despite spending first Diwali since marriage away from home
item.description: Indian boxer Aarti Hooda says she is fit and ready to face Laite Nanovu in the Zeg Boxing Promotion Light Flyweight title fight tomorrow at the Vodafone Arena. Hooda, who is from Haryana, India, says her preparations have been going very well, and she has been working hard to ensure she is ready to fight for the title.
item.content:encoded:
Indian boxer Aarti Hooda says she is fit and ready to face Laite Nanovu in the Zeg Boxing Promotion Light Flyweight title fight tomorrow at the Vodafone Arena.

Hooda, who is from Haryana, India, says her preparations have been going very well, and she has been working hard to ensure she is ready to fight for the title.

She says when she faced Nanovu last year, she was unable to train as much due to an injury but still managed to secure a victory.

Hooda says she is in much better shape this year and is confident heading into tomorrow's fight.

Hindi insert: Hood on if she wins 6th Nov

She says this is her first Diwali since getting married, and although she is away from her family, achieving her dreams and goals remains her priority.

Hooda says she does not feel like she is away from her home country because of the love and support she has received from the Indo-Fijian community and other Fijians.

She also wishes everyone a happy Diwali and thanks the people of Fiji for making her feel welcome.

The Zeg Boxing Promotion event will be held at Vodafone Arena tomorrow, with fights scheduled to begin at 5pm.

item.title: Yasawa confident of challenging defending champions Namosi – Ragadi
item.description: The Yasawa Women's Rugby team is confident that they can put on a strong performance against defending champions Namosi in tomorrow's Pio Bosco Trophy Challenge, despite expecting fewer supporters at the Uprising Sports Centre at Pacific Harbour. Coach Tuliana Ragadi , who hails from Nalawa in Ra, says her team has prepared well throughout the week and is ready for the challenge.
item.content:encoded:
The Yasawa Women's Rugby team is confident that they can put on a strong performance against defending champions Namosi in tomorrow's Pio Bosco Trophy Challenge, despite expecting fewer supporters at the Uprising Sports Centre at Pacific Harbour.

Coach Tuliana Ragadi , who hails from Nalawa in Ra, says her team has prepared well throughout the week and is ready for the challenge.

She says Yasawa have great respect for Namosi, but believes her players have what it takes to deliver a strong performance.

Ragadi says playing in championship matches is nothing new for Yasawa, and she trusts her players to rise to the occasion.

She acknowledges that Namosi are likely to have more supporters at the venue but says this will not discourage her team.

The Yasawa coach says her players are focused on giving their best throughout the full 80 minutes, and understand the importance of remaining united and not underestimating their opponents.

Ragadi says the team are determined to bring the Pio Bosco Trophy home, while Namosi will be looking to retain the title.

Meanwhile, Ragadi is calling on the Yasawa families living in Suva and the Western Division, particularly those near Uprising, to come out and support the team.

She says having families and supporters cheering from the sidelines will give the players extra strength and motivation to perform well.

Yasawa will face Namosi at 3pm tomorrow at the Uprising Sports Centre in Pacific Harbour.

item.title: Bower and Tavatavanawai named on the bench in Scotland clash
item.description: All Blacks with Fijian links, George Bower and Timoci Tavatavanawai have been named on the bench in their Nations Championship opener against Scotland this Sunday. Coach Dave Rennie has made five changes to the side that played Australia, with prop Ethan De Groot at loosehead and Jordie Barrett returns from injury at second five-eighth while Asafo Aumua, Christian Lio-Willie and Anton Segner will
item.content:encoded:
All Blacks with Fijian links, George Bower and Timoci Tavatavanawai have been named on the bench in their Nations Championship opener against Scotland this Sunday.

Coach Dave Rennie has made five changes to the side that played Australia, with prop Ethan De Groot at loosehead and Jordie Barrett returns from injury at second five-eighth while Asafo Aumua, Christian Lio-Willie and Anton Segner will chime in from a very punchy bench.

De Groot will be joined by Captain, Codie Taylor, and Fletcher Newell in the front row.

Locks Scott Barrett and Fabian Holland once again partner up, with Tupou Vaa’i, Peter Lakai and Wallace Sititi continuing to make up Rennie’s preferred loose forward trio without regular captain Ardie Savea.

Cam Roigard starts at halfback with Damian McKenzie at first five-eighth, Jordie Barrett and Quinn Tupaea stay settled in the midfield.

Josh Moorby and Will Jordan head back to the wings and Beauden Barrett continues his second half of the season selection resurgence with Richie Mo’unga on ice for at least one more week.

Joining Aumua, Lio-Willie and Segner on the bench are props George Bower and Pasilio Tosi, halfback Cortez Ratima, power midfielder Timoci Tavatavanawai and experienced outside back Rieko Ioane.

Familiar to the Scottish rugby scene from his tenure as head-coach of Glasgow, Rennie made it clear he was under no illusions about the challenge Scotland present at home.

Rennie says Scotland are a quality side who are very well coached and have built a lot of depth over recent years, and they play a very similar brand of footy to them and they know they will need to be at their best on Saturday.

Scottish mentor Gregor Townsend has named a very experienced squad himself, led by Sione Tuipulotu as one of 10 starting Glasgow Warriors players.

Talented pivot Finn Russell is the most experienced player in Townsend’s 23, preparing for his 96th Scotland cap.

The All Blacks have never lost to Scotland since they first clashed in 1905. Playing each other 33 times, the All Blacks have won 31 tests, with the other two results being draws.

All Blacks: Beauden Barrett, Will Jordan, Quinn Tupaea, Jordie Barrett, Josh Moorby, Damian McKenzie, Cam Roigard, Wallace Sititi, Peter Lakai, Tupou Vaa’i, Fabian Holland, Scott Barrett, Fletcher Newell, Codie Taylor (c), Ethan de Groot.

Reserves: Asafo Aumua, George Bower, Pasilio Tosi, Christian Lio-Willie, Anton Segner, Cortez Ratima, Timoci Tavatavanawai, Rieko Ioane.

The All Blacks will play Scotland at 2.10am Sunday at Murrayfield.

item.title: Khelan and Kwong finish swimming events as Fiji futsal side loses 6-0 to Venezuela
item.description: Fiji swimmers Grace-Elizabeth Khelan and Thaddeus Kwong have completed their events at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, while the women's futsal team has ended its Group A campaign following a 6-0 defeat to Venezuela. In the women's 50-metre backstroke heats, Khelan clocked 32.30 seconds to finish 29th out of 45 swimmers.
item.content:encoded:
Fiji swimmers Grace-Elizabeth Khelan and Thaddeus Kwong have completed their events at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar, Senegal, while the women's futsal team has ended its Group A campaign following a 6-0 defeat to Venezuela.

In the women's 50-metre backstroke heats, Khelan clocked 32.30 seconds to finish 29th out of 45 swimmers.

Kwong recorded a time of 28.04 seconds in the men's 50-metre backstroke heats, placing 16th out of 33 competitors.

In triathlon, Fiji's representative Josiah Crocker was unable to finish the men's event after his bicycle was damaged during the race.

item.title: Former Saint Thomas student Nathan Hughes to make Flying Fijians debut
item.description: Former Saint Thomas High School student and former England international loose forward, Nathan Hughes is set to make his debut for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians after being named in the starting XV to face France in the 2026 Nations Championship. Hughes, who previously represented England at international level, has been handed the number 8 jersey as Fiji prepare to face France at Groupama Stadium
item.content:encoded:
Former Saint Thomas High School student and former England international loose forward, Nathan Hughes is set to make his debut for the FIJI Water Flying Fijians after being named in the starting XV to face France in the 2026 Nations Championship.

Hughes, who previously represented England at international level, has been handed the number 8 jersey as Fiji prepare to face France at Groupama Stadium in Lyon.

His inclusion adds significant experience, power and physicality to a formidable Fijian forward pack that will be expected to match France's intensity and aggression up front.

Captain Tevita Ikanivere will lead the forwards alongside Eroni Mawi, Luke Tagi, Mesake Vocevoce, Isoa Nasilasila, Pita-Gus Sowakula, Kitione Salawa and Hughes .

Meanwhile, the Flying Fijians have assembled an exciting backline featuring several players with experience in France's highly competitive Top 14 competition.

Simione Kuruvoli will start at halfback, partnering flyhalf Isikeli Rabitu, while Jiuta Wainiqolo, Vinaya Habosi, Iosefo Masi, Selestino Ravutaumada and fullback Salesi Rayasi complete the starting backline.

The Flying Fijians will also have experienced players coming off the bench, including Zuriel Togiatama, Peni Ravai, Inoke Ravuwasa, Peceli Yato, Elia Canakaivata, Frank Lomani, Ben Volavola and Sireli Maqala.

With a powerful forward pack and an explosive backline, the Flying Fijians will be determined to make their presence felt against France.

Fiji will face France at 8.10am on Sunday.
